# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, camera batteries and a CPAP for a weekend or longer. Bigger units only make sense if you want to run a fridge or small appliances.

**Weekend tent or car camping (~300Wh)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 300W, 8.3 lb) is PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick for being light and simple. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so look for it at Amazon and other retailers. [Review and buy link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W) is a good choice if you want a stronger inverter (double the Jackery's) and expandability to 572Wh. [Same guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the AC-less "C300 DC". [Same guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W) is the budget pick. [Same guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the small Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low overall. Their strengths are weight and price, so they suit light-duty use. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

**Longer trips, electric cooler, small appliances (~1kWh+)**
- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 35 lb, 5-year warranty) lists at $499. Dealectric reports that code AFF5OFF brought it to $474.05 in a cart test on 2026-10-21. The checkout price is the final word. [Buy at BLUETTI (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). It has no expansion port, and the $599 bundle includes a 100W solar panel. [Details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale for under $530. It's compact and has plenty of ports, but the fan is noisy and capacity is limited. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799) is PowerStationGearLab's pick for van or overland setups. [Guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

**Multi-day off-grid**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It tested at 1,710Wh usable, has 2,200W output and weighs 39 lb. It's under $900 on sale against a $1,499 list price. It can't run a space heater or electric burner for long. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** was WIRED's camping pick ($1,079-$1,199). It's IP65-rated, survives a one-meter drop and has 1,536Wh. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

**My pick:** For most people, the Jackery Explorer 300 Plus or Anker C300 handles a weekend. If you want a cooler or small appliances, the Bluetti AC180 is the better step up.

I only had a direct purchase link for the Bluetti AC180. For the others, the review pages above have the retailer buttons, and prices change, so check the current price before buying. Black Friday is coming up, so prices may drop. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
